samples.summary: Named-style exception writes a real `false` that survives a block-type change / paste, re-creating the #749 dead flag outside the new guard
samples.evidence: `styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:394-418) deliberately KEEPS `italic: false` when the block's named style supplies the key (Heading 6). Nothing re-normalises that run when the block stops supplying it: `Doc.setBlockType` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:456) forwards straight to `store.setBlockType`, which only rewrites `type`/`headingLevel`/`listKind` and leaves `block.inlines` untouched — so Heading 6 → paragraph leaves an explicit `italic:false` in a paragraph whose style supplies nothing, i.e. exactly the dead flag the change exists to eliminate (unmergeable by `inlineStylesEqual`/`normalizeInlines`, and pinned against a later style redefinition). The same residue travels through the internal clipboard, which serialises whole `Block`s with run styles verbatim (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:10-23, 51-60) — copy Heading 6 text, paste into a paragraph, and the `false` lands there. Both paths bypass `Doc.applyInlineStyle`, the only place the demotion happens. Fix belongs either in `setBlockType`/paste normalisation or in a read-side rule that treats a false-with-no-supplying-style as clearable.

samples.summary: Two src call sites write inline styles straight to `DocStore.applyStyles`, bypassing the new `Doc.styleOffAsClear` demotion
samples.evidence: The invariant is enforced only inside `Doc.applyInlineStyle`/`applyInlineStyleToCells` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:377, 431), but `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1095` and `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:907` call `docStore.applyStyles(...)` directly, skipping `Doc` entirely. Today they only write `{ fontSize }`, so no boolean escapes; the guard nevertheless sits one layer above the store interface that anyone can call (`DocStore.applyStyles`, packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:90), so a future boolean batch write would silently store `false` again. Consider demoting inside the store helper (`store/block-helpers.applyInlineStyle`) instead of in `Doc`.

samples.summary: Agent charters and the hunt-oracle verifier still assert the pre-change docs behaviour ("#749 stores italic:false")
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/charters-ui/doc-writer.md:117` ("#749 stores `italic:false`"), `scripts/agent/charters-ui/sheet-author.md:85` and :180 ("this is where the sheet surface DIFFERS from docs, where the same round trip leaves an explicit `false` behind (#749, #793). Do not carry that expectation across.") and `packages/frontend/scripts/verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:592` (same claim in a comment guarding the sheets round-trip assertion) all describe behaviour this change removes. None is enforced by CI (markdown under scripts/, and a comment), so they will quietly steer agents/oracles to the old contract. Mirrored copies exist under `.trusted/scripts/agent/...`.

samples.summary: Clearing keys makes cache/Tree inline-structure divergence more frequent, and `insertText` still reads a run style by cache index
samples.evidence: `applyInlineStyleHelper` now deletes the key and `normalizeInlines` re-merges the run into its neighbours, so the cached block collapses to one inline while the Yorkie Tree keeps the three inline nodes the split produced (`applyStyleInTree`'s Step 6 only deletes EMPTY inlines, packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1892-1900). `insertText` then resolves `cacheResolved.inlineIndex` against the cache and reads `block.inlines[cacheResolved.inlineIndex]` (line 1571) while the actual edit uses the tree-resolved index (line 1602) — with diverged structures the style read for the image branch / empty-block branch can come from a different run than the one edited. Divergence was already possible pre-change (re-applying an identical style also merges in cache only), so this raises frequency rather than introducing the hazard; flagged because the toggle-off path is now the hottest producer of it.

finding.summary: Named-style exception writes a real `false` that survives a block-type change / paste, re-creating the #749 dead flag outside the new guard
finding.evidence: `styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:394-418) deliberately KEEPS `italic: false` when the block's named style supplies the key (Heading 6). Nothing re-normalises that run when the block stops supplying it: `Doc.setBlockType` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:456) forwards straight to `store.setBlockType`, which only rewrites `type`/`headingLevel`/`listKind` and leaves `block.inlines` untouched — so Heading 6 → paragraph leaves an explicit `italic:false` in a paragraph whose style supplies nothing, i.e. exactly the dead flag the change exists to eliminate (unmergeable by `inlineStylesEqual`/`normalizeInlines`, and pinned against a later style redefinition). The same residue travels through the internal clipboard, which serialises whole `Block`s with run styles verbatim (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:10-23, 51-60) — copy Heading 6 text, paste into a paragraph, and the `false` lands there. Both paths bypass `Doc.applyInlineStyle`, the only place the demotion happens. Fix belongs either in `setBlockType`/paste normalisation or in a read-side rule that treats a false-with-no-supplying-style as clearable.

verdict.reason: Every claimed fact checks out. styleOffAsClear keeps an explicit `false` when the block's named style supplies the key (document.ts:405-417, guard at :413), and heading-6 really does supply `italic: true` (named-styles.ts:91), so the exception is reachable. Doc.setBlockType (document.ts:447-458) forwards to MemoryStore.setBlockType (memory.ts:242-271), which rewrites only type/headingLevel/listKind/listLevel and block spacing and never touches block.inlines — so Heading 6 → paragraph leaves an explicit italic:false in a block whose style supplies nothing. That residue is a real dead flag: inlineStylesEqual compares italic strictly (types.ts:404-407) so normalizeInlines (block-helpers.ts:76-81) cannot re-merge the run, and visitStyledRunsInRange layers defaults under run style (range-runs.ts:57,64) so the false pins the run against a later style redefinition — the exact #749 hazard the new code documents (document.ts:387-392). The internal clipboard carries the same residue: serializeClipboard/serializeBlocks stringify whole Blocks verbatim (clipboard.ts:10-13,30-36) from copy/cut at text-editor.ts:1056,1085, and paste reads them back unmodified at text-editor.ts:1204-1206. I found no re-normalisation guard on either path and no read-side clearable-false rule, so there is no already-guarded basis; the issue is state escaping a new write-time guard through untouched call paths, which is squarely this lens's lane.

finding.summary: Hyperlink runs are a second place where an explicit `false` carries information, and `styleOffAsClear` does not exempt it — toggling underline off on a link is now a visual no-op.
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:387-391 renders `let showUnderline = style.underline ?? false; if (style.href) { ... if (style.underline === undefined) showUnderline = true; }`. So for a run with `href`, an ABSENT `underline` key means "paint the link default underline", and only an explicit `underline: false` suppresses it. `Doc.styleOffAsClear` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:398-417) preserves `false` only when the block's *named-style* defaults set the key (`resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), ...)`); a hyperlink in a normal paragraph has no named-style underline, so the `false` is demoted to `undefined`. Result: selecting a link and toggling underline off (Cmd+U / toolbar U, whose write funnels through `Doc.applyInlineStyle`) now clears the key and paint-layout immediately re-applies the link's default underline — the user can no longer remove a link's underline, and the raw-style-based `getRangeStyleSummary` will report underline OFF while the canvas paints it ON (the exact toolbar/render disagreement issue #715 was about). The fix belongs on the new code: the exemption in `styleOffAsClear` needs to also keep `false` for `underline` when the slice being written carries `href` (or the paint default has to move into the resolved-style layer).

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the repo. paint-layout.ts:387-391 gives an explicit `underline: false` semantic meaning on href runs (absent key => paint link default underline; only explicit false suppresses). Doc.styleOffAsClear (document.ts:399-418) rewrites `underline: false` to `undefined` unless the block's named style supplies underline (`resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), ...)`, line 410-413); document.ts contains no `href` reference at all. mergeInlineStyle (block-helpers.ts:316-325) then deletes the key entirely. Both underline-off entry points reach it: toolbar (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:404 -> editor.ts:1031 doc.applyInlineStyle) and Cmd+U (text-editor.ts:887 -> toggleStyle inversion at 2881-2893 -> applyStyleToSelection -> text-editor.ts:2935 doc.applyInlineStyle). Link creation stores only `{href: url}` (editor.ts:2962/2981/2997), so no explicit underline and no named-style default exists to trigger the exemption. Result: turning underline off on a hyperlink is now a stored-key clear that paint-layout immediately re-underlines, while the raw-style summary reports OFF. This is an out-of-diff consumer broken by a changed contract on an exported symbol — in-lane and major.

finding.summary: Format painter (Cmd+Shift+C / Cmd+Alt+V) silently loses its ability to REMOVE B/I/U/S now that toggle-off clears the key instead of storing `false`
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:869 captures the painter buffer as the RAW caret run style (`this.styleBuffer = { ...this.getStyleAtCursor() }`, and `getStyleAtCursor` is documented at :2942-2949 as raw run style), and :1013 applies it via `applyStyleToSelection(range, this.styleBuffer)` → `Doc.applyInlineStyle` → `mergeInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:316-325), which only merges keys that are PRESENT in the patch. Before this PR a run that the user had un-bolded carried an explicit `bold: false`, so copying its formatting onto bold text un-bolded it. With `styleOffAsClear` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:399-418) the key is deleted from the run, so the painter buffer no longer contains `bold`/`italic`/`underline`/`strikethrough` at all and pasting the format onto bold/italic target text leaves the target's formatting in place. Neither call site was updated to compensate (e.g. by materialising explicit `false`/`undefined` for the boolean keyset when capturing). Fix belongs at the painter capture site, or by having the painter capture the full boolean keyset.

verdict.reason: Every link in the reviewer's chain checks out. text-editor.ts:865-870 captures the format-painter buffer as the RAW caret run style via getStyleAtCursor (2942-2951) -> caretInlineStyle (caret-style.ts:46-66), which returns only keys present on the run (no boolean keyset materialised). text-editor.ts:1005-1016 applies it via applyStyleToSelection (2921-2940) -> Doc.applyInlineStyle (document.ts:375-380) -> mergeInlineStyle (block-helpers.ts:316-325), a spread-merge plus deletion of explicitly-undefined keys, so keys ABSENT from the patch leave the target's formatting untouched. document.ts:399-418 (styleOffAsClear, called at 377 and 431) rewrites a boolean set to false into undefined (key deleted) unless the block's named style supplies it, and toggleStyle does send explicit false (text-editor.ts:2880-2893, applied at 2903). So a run the user explicitly un-bolded no longer stores bold:false, the painter buffer no longer carries bold/italic/underline/strikethrough, and Cmd+Alt+V onto bold text can no longer un-bold it. styleBuffer has only four references (89, 869, 1009, 1013) and none compensates; no guard makes this unreachable and the trigger is a documented shortcut. This is a consumer outside the diff left inconsistent by a changed stored-representation contract, in the blast-radius lane. No named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Toggle-off now emits a Yorkie `removeStyleByPath` op on the hottest editing path (B/I/U/S); if Yorkie history cannot reverse TreeStyleRemove, Cmd+Z after a toggle-off silently stops restoring the flag
finding.evidence: With the demotion in `Doc.styleOffAsClear`, every B/I/U/S off-toggle now reaches `YorkieDocStore.applyStyleInTree` with the key set to `undefined`, so `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:144-163) returns the attr and `tree.removeStyleByPath(...)` runs at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1881 — previously only `styleByPath` ran for a toggle-off (the `false` was serialized), and `removeStyleByPath` was reached only by the rare removeLink / clear-formatting paths. Docs undo is Yorkie-history based (`this.doc.history.undo()` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2611), so the reversibility of the removeStyle op is now load-bearing for the most common formatting action in the product. I could not verify the SDK's reverse-op support from this checkout (the Yorkie SDK is not installed in node_modules here); confirming needs a collab/integration run that toggles bold off and then undoes it against a real Yorkie doc. Fix, if real, belongs in the Yorkie store (emit a compensating style write) rather than in the new Doc code.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is real — `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:144-163) returns the attr for an explicitly-undefined key and `tree.removeStyleByPath` runs at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1888, with undo going through `this.doc.history.undo()` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2618. But the claimed consequence (undo silently stops restoring the flag) is contradicted by an in-repo counterexample that runs against the REAL Yorkie SDK, not a mock: tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2 imports `@yorkie-js/sdk` (pinned 0.7.16 at packages/frontend/package.json:93), :28-36 builds a real `yorkie.Document`/`yorkie.Tree` and the real `YorkieDocStore` (no `vi.mock` of the SDK in this file — the only such mock is in src/app/documents/__tests__/apply-imported-content.test.ts:29), and :214-228 performs exactly `bold:true` → `bold:undefined` (the removeStyleByPath path) → `undo()` asserting `bold === true` restored → `redo()` asserting it cleared. That file is in the default vitest include set (packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:266-271), so the reversibility the finding calls "unverified and load-bearing" is asserted on every test run; an SDK that could not reverse TreeStyleRemove would produce a failing test on the same gate rather than a silent Cmd+Z regression. The design doc records the same behaviour at docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:276-278. The reviewer themselves noted they could not verify the SDK behaviour; the repository resolves it against them.
